## Overview

Carpinteria Salt Marsh is the field site for week 7. Carp Salt Marsh and Devereux Slough (at NCOS/COPR) are examples of estuaries - specifically salt marshes - which are key coastal ecosystems. In this independent field trip option, you will visit another estuary close to campus: Goleta Slough. Choose this option if you are interested in ecosystems bridging marine and freshwater aquatic systems.

You will turn in a **hard copy** of this assignment in class. If you don't want to turn in your entire notebook, do this assignment _separately_ from your notebook. 

## Locations

You will walk, bike, or otherwise travel to three points relating to Goleta Slough, all within 1 mile of Henley Gate: 1) Tecolotito Creek Bridge, 2) pond at Atascadero Creek bend, and 3) the mouth of the slough.

## Assignment overview

:::{.callout-tip title="Don't forget your metadata!"}

:::

### a. Create a species account.

At each of these points, identify as many species as possible _in one taxonomic group_ to characterize the habitat in which you find yourself. 

Take _at least_ 15 minutes for your species accounts. 

### b. Conduct an observation.

Choose _two_ points at which you want to closely observe an organism, species, or interaction.

Take _at least_ for minutes on your observation.

### c. Write your post-field day reflection.

In your reflection, compare what you saw at Goleta Slough with Carpinteria Salt Marsh and Devereux Slough. Discuss how they compare in:

- water source
- water level
- species richness (i.e. number of species)
- community composition (i.e. species present)

Discuss _why_ you may have observed any similarities or differences (e.g. shared habitats, common plants, time of day of visit).

## Checklist

By the due date, you should have:

- [ ] metadata for your field day
- [ ] species accounts for all three points on the map
- [ ] an observation from two points of your choosing
- [ ] a post-field day reflection 

You will turn in a **hard copy** of your species accounts, observations, and reflections in class on Tuesday the 17th of November.
